G1.comment: Opens and renders with no errors. Needs internet for three.js from unpkg.

G2.comment: No lower angle limit, so the camera can go below the ground, and the 45 m zoom pulls out until the grove floats in a white void.

G3.comment: 340 instanced stalks, 3,400 leaf cards, one shadow map and bloom. Likely above 30 fps on a laptop, not measured on one.

1.comment: A bar with a hint and three buttons (Match Photo Angle, Ground Walk View, Wind) sits over the scene.

2.comment: Stalks and leaves sway from load with no input.

3.comment: Low upward view with the stalks converging on the sky, as in the photo, though the convergence is more evenly radial.

4.comment: Stalk spacing and density are close to the photo.

5.comment: A white haze turns the palette pale grey green. The photo's saturated yellow green and deep green are missing.

6.comment: No path and no brushwood fence.

7.comment: Bright diffuse light from above, as in the photo, though the haze washes it out.

8.comment: Nodes are modelled as small flares with a dark ring in the texture, at regular intervals.

10.comment: Stalks lean at slightly varied angles toward the opening.

11.comment: The canopy is made of narrow lance shaped leaves in sprays.

12.comment: The ground is a flat, plain dark green disc.

13.comment: Zooming out shows the whole grove as a ball floating in white, with clear edges.

14.comment: Leaves cast no shadows, so there is no dappled light on the stalks or the ground.

15.comment: Fog and bloom give soft depth between the stalks.

16.comment: Leaves glow with an emissive tint against the sky.

17.comment: No area between the stalks is fully black.

18.comment: The culm texture has a waxy roughness map, mottling and slight colour variation between stalks.

19.comment: Leaves read as lit through, using an emissive tint rather than real translucency.

20.comment: The ground is a flat colour with no soil, leaf or stone texture.

21.comment: No unwanted roll. Verticals converge as in the upward photo.

22.comment: The canopy sways in the wind.

23.comment: Sway grows with height, so stalks bend more at the top than at the base.

24.comment: Wind is a sum of steady sine waves, with no gusts.

25.comment: No falling leaves or dust particles.

26.comment: Motion runs on a continuous clock with no visible jumps.

27.comment: All 340 stalks share one mesh with the same bow, so identical stalks stand side by side.

28.comment: No popping seen in the captures. Not checked on a real GPU.

29.comment: Leaf cards up to about 4 m wide sit at random angles among the stalks and sway on their own, so they cut through stalks.

30.comment: Too hazy and too pale to pass for the photo at a glance.

G1.comment: Opens and renders with no errors. Needs internet for three.js from unpkg.

G2.comment: The polar limit keeps the camera above the water, and the 300 m zoom limit stays well inside the 10 km ocean.

G3.comment: One shadow map, a terrain mesh, a reflective water plane and simple primitives. Likely above 30 fps on a laptop, not measured on one.

1.comment: A controls hint (Left Click: Rotate, Right Click: Pan, Scroll: Zoom) sits over the scene.

2.comment: The water surface moves from load, with no input.

3.comment: The default view looks up a snow slope with the lighthouse small at the top and the horizon high. The photo looks across the rocks with the horizon in the lower third.

4.comment: White octagonal tapered tower with a red lantern, as in the photo.

5.comment: The headland is a snow dome with a few boulders. The photo's exposed grey granite is almost entirely missing.

6.comment: The ocean is visible beyond the headland, though it reads pale grey rather than blue.

7.comment: The sky is a pale white grey, not the photo's clear deep blue.

8.comment: Slender tapered octagonal shaft, close to the photo's proportions.

9.comment: The lantern has glass panes and a railed gallery deck.

10.comment: The boulders are smooth blobs with no visible cracks or fissures.

11.comment: The tower sits on a plinth on a flattened summit, flush with the ground.

12.comment: The ocean plane reaches the horizon in every direction, with no visible edge.

13.comment: One sun with a shadow map, and every shadow falls the same way.

14.comment: The tower is not blown out and shows soft shading on its far side.

15.comment: The sea fades into a pale haze at the horizon.

16.comment: No pure black or clipped white pixels in the default view.

17.comment: Clean flat white paint with no grime, streaks or wear.

18.comment: Snow reads as snow, but there is almost no exposed rock, and none of it is dark and wet at the waterline.

19.comment: The lantern glass is highly transmissive and reflects an environment map of the sky.

20.comment: The water reflects the sky with a Fresnel falloff, but its colour doesn't shift with depth.

22.comment: The sea is a flat plane with a scrolling normal map. No waves roll in and there are no wave heights.

23.comment: No waves break on the rocks, and there is no foam or spray.

25.comment: Nothing shows wind: no drifting snow, no spray, no moving grass.

26.comment: The water normals scroll continuously, with no visible jumps.

27.comment: No obvious repeating pattern on the sea in the captures.

28.comment: There are no spray particles in the scene.

29.comment: The water meets the shore along a hard line, with no foam.

30.comment: The pale sky and sea and the smooth snow dome make the paused frame read as CG, not as the photo.

G1.comment: Opens and renders with no errors. Needs internet for three.js from unpkg.

G2.comment: The polar limit keeps the camera above the water and the zoom stops at 26 m, so the camera stays in the scene.

G3.comment: One bird mesh, one shadow map and a reflective water plane. Likely above 30 fps on a laptop, not measured on one.

1.comment: A controls hint (Drag to Orbit, Scroll to Zoom, Right-Drag to Pan) sits over the scene.

2.comment: The water moves and the bird bobs from load, with no input.

3.comment: Side view at the bird's height with the bird filling most of the frame, though it sits right of centre.

4.comment: One flamingo stands in calm water, mid-stride with one leg forward.

5.comment: Coral neck and body, pink legs, black flight feathers and a pale beak with a black tip, as in the photo.

6.comment: A sharp horizon splits a dark blue sky from pale water. The photo is one soft, even blue with no horizon.

7.comment: The sun comes from the front right, as in the photo.

8.comment: The neck forms the S curve with the head and beak pointing down.

9.comment: Long thin legs with a backward-bending joint and a small body. The feet are simple cones rather than webbed.

10.comment: The wing is partly raised, with black flight feathers fanning out behind.

11.comment: The feet meet the water surface, with a ripple ring at the forward foot.

12.comment: The bird is modelled on both sides, with no holes, and the water reaches the horizon.

13.comment: Shading follows the body form, with a lit side and a softer shaded side.

14.comment: No pure black or clipped white pixels in the default view.

15.comment: The background is a sharp sky gradient over a horizon, not the photo's soft, out-of-focus blue.

16.comment: The body and neck are smooth sculpted shells with a fine bump, not layered plumage.

17.comment: The legs are matte with darker joints, and the beak tip is glossy black.

18.comment: The water is a smooth, glossy surface with a Fresnel reflection.

19.comment: The bird and its legs reflect in the water.

21.comment: One ring at the forward foot pulses in place. Ripples don't spread out from the legs.

22.comment: The bird bobs by 8 mm and the neck turns by a fraction of a degree, too little to see.

23.comment: A scrolling normal map moves small wavelets across the water.

24.comment: Motion runs on a continuous clock with no visible jumps.

25.comment: There is a single ring that keeps a hard edge, not concentric rings that fade with distance.

26.comment: The legs don't cut through the body or the water in the captures.

27.comment: No visible texture seams or repeats on the plumage.

28.comment: The outline is clean geometry, with no cut-out edges or halos.

29.comment: The horizon, the smooth shell body and the simple legs make the paused frame read as CG, not as the photo.

30.comment: The body casts soft shadows under the wing and along the neck, from the same sun.

G1.comment: Opens and renders with no errors. Needs internet for three.js from unpkg.

G2.comment: The camera stays above the table, but zooming out shows the edge of the tablecloth and a black void behind it.

G3.comment: Two shadow-casting lights, bloom and depth-of-field passes and dense geometry, the heaviest of the five. Likely above 30 fps on a laptop, not measured on one.

1.comment: A bar with a hint and two buttons (Macro DoF, Hero Angle) sits over the scene.

2.comment: Nothing moves. The animation loop only updates the camera.

3.comment: Close up from slightly above with the stack centred on the plate, as in the photo.

4.comment: Three slices are stacked and slightly offset.

5.comment: Banana slices sit between the layers and a few lie on the plate, though fewer than in the photo.

6.comment: Blueberries sit on top of the stack and around its base.

7.comment: The stack sits on a dark round plate on a grey-brown cloth.

8.comment: Powdered sugar is dusted over the plate and lightly over the toast.

9.comment: The slices are glossy slabs with wavy, ridged edges. They read as crackers rather than thick bread with a rounded crust.

10.comment: Banana slices are round discs with the faint seeded pattern in the centre.

11.comment: Blueberries are round, vary slightly in size and show the star-shaped crown.

12.comment: Fruit and toast rest on each other and on the plate, with nothing floating.

13.comment: Zooming out shows the edge of the tablecloth and a black void beyond it.

14.comment: The key light comes from the front left. The photo is lit from behind, with the warm highlights on the far edges.

15.comment: A depth-of-field pass softens the cloth behind the plate, though less than in the photo.

16.comment: Fruit, toast and the plate cast soft shadows.

17.comment: A strip of pure black void shows above the tablecloth at the top of the default view.

18.comment: Syrup runs in glossy, transmissive amber rivulets and drops down the crusts.

19.comment: The toast is an even glossy orange with no uneven browning, and the porous crumb doesn't show.

20.comment: Blueberries have a dusty, matte look with soft highlights.

21.comment: Banana slices look moist and slightly translucent.

22.comment: The plate reads as dark ceramic with a soft sheen, and the cloth has a woven texture.

23.comment: The plate and the table are level.

24.comment: The syrup drips are modelled but don't move.

25.comment: There is no steam or haze.

26.comment: There is no motion to judge.

27.comment: Each blueberry and banana slice is generated from its own seed, so no identical copies sit side by side.

28.comment: Banana discs about 0.23 thick sit tilted in roughly 0.22 gaps between the slices, so they cut into the toast.

29.comment: The sugar reads as fine grains and a soft dusting, not sprite squares.

30.comment: The cracker-like slabs and the black void above the table make the paused frame read as CG, not as the photo.
